name: Bloom probabilistic membership filter
definition: For an m-bit zero array B and k distinct addresses H(x), insertion sets B[i]←1 for i∈H(x); query Q(x)=∏_{i∈H(x)} B[i]. With T=Σ_i B[i], Pr(Q(x)=1 | B)=choose(T,k)/choose(m,k) for an independent uniform k-subset query of a nonmember
variables: m bit capacity; k addresses per key; H(x) stable address subset; T occupied bit count; Q binary query result; choose binomial coefficient (zero if T<k)
assumptions: Integers 1≤k≤m; insertion only, stable distinct address mapping, intact bit state and consistent key representation. Probability formula additionally requires the absent query key's address set to be uniform among k-subsets and independent of the constructed filter
limitations: Positive results can be false; negatives exclude previously inserted keys only under the stated intact insertion-only model. Saturation yields all positives. Probability is conditional on occupied state, not a guarantee for adaptive queries or arbitrary hashes. No deletion, exact count or exact membership recovery
failure_conditions: Invalid dimensions or non-distinct or inconsistent addresses
Lost or cleared bits; treating positive answers as proof
Claiming the conditional probability without its independence assumption
computation: Initialize all m bits to zero. For each insertion obtain k distinct stable addresses and set each bit. On query test every addressed bit and return negative if any is zero; otherwise return possible membership. Duplicate insertions leave the state unchanged. If an exact positive decision is required, consult an authoritative set. For the stated random-address model compute the conditional ratio using the observed occupied count

source.citation: Bloom (1970), Space/time trade-offs in hash coding with allowable errors, Communications of the ACM 13(7), 422–426, Method 2, p. 423. DOI 10.1145/362686.362692. https://crystal.uta.edu/~mcguigan/cse6350/papers/Bloom.pdf ; conditional occupancy ratio independently derived

application: General approximate set membership; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Key stream, bit array capacity and hash functions.
incompatible_methods: Treating a positive query as proof of membership
mechanism_note: Inserted keys retain every addressed bit by monotonicity. Under independent uniform distinct query addresses, exactly choose(T,k) of choose(m,k) equally likely subsets lie wholly in the occupied set. This is conditional on the bit pattern and differs from the common independent-with-replacement approximation. Boolean set-membership screening differs from Count–Min numerical frequency estimation.

name: Count Sketch signed frequency estimator
definition: C[j,h_j(x)]←C[j,h_j(x)]+s_j(x)u; Z_j(x)=s_j(x)C[j,h_j(x)]; f_hat(x)=median_j Z_j(x). E[Z_j]=f_x; Var(Z_j)=Σ_{y≠x} f_y²/b. For odd d and V=Σ_{y≠x} f_y²/b>0, Pr(|f_hat−f_x|>2√V)≤exp(−d/8)
variables: C signed counter matrix; b buckets per row; d odd row count; h_j bucket hash; s_j sign hash into {−1,+1}; u signed increment; f_y net frequency; Z_j row estimate; V row variance
assumptions: Finite key universe, fixed update vector and query independent of hashes, exact arithmetic; b≥1 and odd d≥1. Pairwise independent uniform bucket hashes and pairwise independent unbiased signs, sign and bucket functions independent, rows mutually independent
limitations: Two-sided additive error depends on other keys' squared frequencies; median is not asserted unbiased. Bound is for a fixed query, not adaptive queries, and does not recover unknown keys or guarantee a top-k list. O(bd) counters and d hash evaluations per update or query plus median computation
failure_conditions: Invalid dimensions, counter overflow or nonfinite weights
Hash assumptions not met or applying one-sided Count–Min error bounds
Reporting an approximate signed estimate as an exact count
computation: Initialize zero counters and select independent hash and sign functions with recorded parameters. For every signed update add its sign-adjusted weight to the addressed cell in each row. For the supplied query multiply each addressed counter by the query sign and return the middle of the d sorted values. If V=0 each row is exact almost surely. Identically configured sketches may be added or subtracted componentwise; different hash configurations are incompatible

source.citation: Charikar, Chen and Farach-Colton (2002), Finding frequent items in data streams, ICALP, LNCS 2380, 693–703, sections 3.2, 4 and 4.2. DOI 10.1007/3-540-45465-9_59. https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/spring04/cos598B/bib/CharikarCF.pdf ; fixed-query signed L2 bound independently derived

application: General signed streaming frequency estimation; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Key and update stream, bucket and sign hashes, counter dimensions.
incompatible_methods: Applying Count–Min one-sided guarantee to signed estimation
mechanism_note: Expand Z_j−f_x as Σ_{y≠x} f_y s_j(x)s_j(y)1{h_j(y)=h_j(x)}. Independent unbiased pairwise signs cancel cross terms since s_j(x)²=1; uniform pairwise bucket hashes yield the stated variance. Chebyshev bounds a bad row by 1/4 and Hoeffding bounds a majority of bad independent rows by exp(−d/8). Signed collision cancellation and median estimation differ from nonnegative minimum estimation.
